newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries end off, data fan rate hike fears.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries end off, data fan rate hike fears.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries closed sharply lower in a nervous abbreviated session as fears of an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve mounted after the release of a new batch of stronger-than-expected economic data.

The 6-3/4 percent benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond ended down 30/32 at 95-14/32. Its yield jumped to 7.12 percent, the highest mark in almost seven weeks, from the 7.04 percent registered on Thursday's close.
The market shut at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT on Friday following a recommendation of the Public Securities Association (PSA).
Trading will remain closed on Monday as the market observes the Labor Day holiday.
Analysts said the sentiment now is that a recent slew of data this week dramatically increased the odds for a Federal Reserve tightening of monetary policy before year end.
"There are many people thinking the Fed will have to raise interest rates because the economy is very strong," said Gary Thayer, senior economist at A.G. Edwards & Sons Inc.
The Fed last changed monetary policy in January, when it cut the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to the current target of 5.25 percent.
Preliminary results of a Reuters survey point to an NAPM reading of 52.5 in August compared to 50.2 in July.
"We're getting bombarded ... by much stronger than expected data, and that was especially true with the Chicago PMI," said John Canavan, market analyst at Stone and McCarthy Research Associates Inc.

On top of that, the market took in a surprising 1.9 percent rise in July factory orders against a revised 0.7 percent drop in June. The University of Michigan August final index of consumer sentiment also cast a shadow on the market by rising to 95.3 compared to 94.7 in the final July index.

Comments by Federal Reserve governor Lawrence Lindsey that the U.S. economy appears, on balance, to be "a little bit on the strong side" was also seen as negative. He added the Fed will not curb growth provided inflation remains in check.
The three-month Treasury bill closed up six basis points at 5.15 percent. The six-month bill was up seven points at 5.27 percent. The year bill rose 11 points to 5.59 percent.

The two-year note closed off 6/32 at 99-19/32, yielding 6.34 percent. The five-year note traded off 14/32 at 99-1/32 to yield 6.73 percent. The ten-year note closed down 21/32 at 100-12/32, yielding 6.95 percent. -- 212-859-1676
